title: I spent 3 years building an AI Dungeon Master because I wanted to play D&D whenever I felt like it
author: tschilpi
selftext:
I wanted to make a character, gather a party and go on an adventure without spending a week figuring out when everyone was free.



But the problem I kept running into with AI RPGs was that the world would slowly fall apart. NPCs forgot things. Quests contradicted themselves. A successful roll sounded impressive, but it wasn't always clear whether anything had actually changed.



So I ended up building the world underneath the Dungeon Master.



The game tracks characters, inventory, quests and combat. AI interprets what you want to attempt and narrates what happens in that world.



One of my favourite moments was finding an adventurer NPC buying up troll oil in a shop while I was busy questing. I asked why.



“Trolls.”



I kept asking. She explained that she needed to burn them because they regenerate health too quickly. Fire stopping regeneration is implemented in the game, so she'd put together a plan that could actually work lol.



That's the kind of thing I've spent three years trying to build: the freedom of a D&D session, with an authored visual world and tactical party combat like a classic CRPG.



It's called Lore & Legends Maker. You explore, recruit companions, argue with NPCs and try plans that a dialogue menu wouldn't give you.



I use Claude Code and Codex for development. Keeping world state separate from narration has also made testing more useful: I can check what the game actually changed after an improvised action, then compare that with what the DM said happened. Getting those two to agree is still a lot of the work.



Still an alpha, and there's plenty to fix. But the current version is free to play, and I'd love to hear what you try—and where it breaks.



Attached gameplay is from another encounter in the current alpha.



Play: [https://www.llmsaga.com/](https://www.llmsaga.com/)

Discord: [https://discord.gg/Cr3pQx6SXE](https://discord.gg/Cr3pQx6SXE)

comments.author: ChubbyFrogGames
comments.body: I have tried it at a minimal time frame here, probably 5-10 minutes. The whole making character, choosing your stats etc is too slow for people. You need to add a randomizer for everything. Even the backstory for the characters etc. Then people can jump in quicker and see if it's something for them or not. I will continue to play for 2 or 3 days and come back with more :)

replies.author: tschilpi
replies.body:
Hey, thanks for giving it a shot! :)

I agree that character creation could be a bit more compact and accessible. 

It’s a tricky balance because some players really enjoy customizing every little detail, while others just want to jump straight into the adventure.

Having a quick start / randomize everything option could actually be a great solution!

Really appreciate the feedback, and looking forward to hearing what you think after playing some more :D

replies.author: ChubbyFrogGames
replies.body: Yeah I know what you mean. I also want an indepth experience etc. But for me, and I think many other people, they are busy, they might check the game out while they commute and just want to see what it's all about, so a randomizer to get you going quickly is absolutely the answer here!

comments.author: xblackout_
comments.body: Really cool and beautiful work! What's the plan next?

replies.author: tschilpi
replies.body:
Thanks!! 😁

Right now I’m focusing on polishing the core gameplay, fixing inconsistencies and expanding the adventures.

Longer term, I’d love to make it possible to run existing open-source adventures or create your own adventures with the engine. We were actually just discussing that in the community haha

There’s also a co-op mode in the works so people can eventually go on adventures together!

comments.author: CubersumGame
comments.body:
I was actually just wondering recently why there still isn’t a decent AI Dungeon Master (DM) for running games when you want to play solo. All that exists is the completely nonsensical \*AI Dungeon\* and a few scripts on GitHub designed to assist already-established gaming groups.

This looks really cool!

It would also be great to have an auto-translation feature or a language selection option- after all, it makes no difference to an LLM which language it writes in.

comments.author: revel911
comments.body:
I had an idea for your game …. A module / story converter. Upload a pdf and it pulls out the story, npc’s rooms, and ect… and builds a story for your characters to play with and adds it as a book on the shelf. 

This way the potential is limitless as long as you have a solid foundation vs up to you to also make stories.
